additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food in a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control and significant distress, but without regular compensatory behaviors such as purging or excessive exercise. Episodes are often associated with eating rapidly, eating when not physically hungry, eating alone due to embarrassment, and experiencing shame, guilt, or disgust afterward. The disorder typically follows a chronic or relapsing course, often emerging in late adolescence or early adulthood, and is frequently linked to dieting history, negative affect, and difficulties with emotion regulation. It is distinguished from bulimia nervosa by the absence of compensatory behaviors and from normative overeating by the frequency of episodes, the sense of loss of control, and the marked psychological distress and impairment.

patient.personality: Brandon is energetic, social, and curious, with a spontaneous, improvisational style that sometimes leaves him disorganized and living very much in the moment.
patient.stressor: Over the past year, Brandon picked up longer-haul routes and extra shifts to prove himself for a supervisory logistics role, which meant irregular hours, skipped meals, and relying heavily on truck-stop food and late-night takeout. His usual casual enjoyment of grilling and trying new foods gradually shifted into using food as a way to break up boredom and loneliness on the road, especially after stressful deliveries or arguments with dispatch. During the three months before seeking help, a particularly demanding contract with tight deadlines left him chronically sleep-deprived and wired, and he began capping off runs with increasingly large, solitary meals that he rationalized as a reward for the grind, even when they left him feeling physically awful and sluggish for his next shift. When he noticed he was timing his routes around certain fast-food spots, feeling embarrassed about how he was eating, and that this pattern was starting to interfere with his basketball games and energy at work, he went to his primary care provider, who referred him for a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep eating past the point where I feel stuffed and uncomfortable, and I don't seem to be able to stop myself.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Lately on my way back from a long run, I’ll hit a drive‑thru and order like two burgers, a large fries, nuggets, a shake and then still grab snacks at the next truck stop, and I put it all away in one sitting in the cab like it’s a normal dinner, even though I know most people would be full halfway through that.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like something in my brain just shuts off—I'll be telling myself, 'dude, stop, you’re already full,' but my hands just keep unwrapping another sandwich or reaching into the chip bag until suddenly everything’s gone and I’m sitting there wondering how I even ate all that.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: When I get back to the truck at night, I tear into the food so fast I barely chew or taste it, just shoveling it in between sips of soda, and before I even finish checking my messages the whole pile of food is gone and I almost don’t remember eating it.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: More and more, I end up eating until my stomach feels rock hard and stretched, like I have to lean the driver’s seat back because it hurts to sit up straight and I’m scared to bend over to grab something in case I throw up.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: After one of those nights, when I’m lying in the sleeper sweating and too full to sleep, I just feel gross and pissed at myself, thinking, 'you idiot, you did it again, no wonder you’re dragging at work and skipping ball with the guys.'
